'''''Plectranthus hadiensis''''' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] plant of the family [[Lamiaceae]].

== Description ==
''Plectranthus hadiensis'' is a perennial herbaceous [[shrub]] with pubescent and semi-succulent stems, and a straight to decumbent habit. Its height varies 50 cm to 1.5 m (30–59 in), with a maximum base diameter of 1m (39 in). The [[Leaf|leaves]] of the plant are arranged alternately on the plant's stem, they have coarse textures; an ovate shape; densely woolly-tomentose;  are apex acute to rounded, cuneate with subcordate base; and a superficial to fairly crenate-dentate margin. The petiole is 10 to 40 mm long. The terminal inflorescences of the plant are simple and have 1 to 2 pairs of lateral branches near the base. The flowers of the plant are generally in shades of mauve to purple (occasionally white), and are bilabiated with a tube-shaped corolla of 8 to 15 mm that widens from the base, finely pubescent and with glands on the lips.

There are three varieties of ''P. hadiensis'':

* Variety ''hadiensis'', distributed in coastal and midland areas of the [[KwaZulu-Natal]] woodlands and the east of [[South Africa]];
* Variety ''tomentosus'', in semi-coastal zones from the [[Great Kei River]] to the KwaZulu-Natal coast.
* Variety ''woodii'', distributed in arid habitats in eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal.

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is found in [[Transkei]], Natal, [[Eswatini]], the Transvaal, eastern tropical Africa, [[Somalia]] and the southern [[Arabian Peninsula]]. The plant can be found on the fringes of forests, in dry forests and amongst rocks in grasslands and lowlands.<ref name="jstor2">[http://plants.jstor.org/stable/10.5555/al.ap.flora.flosa001150167104001 JSTOR]</ref>

== Cultivation and uses ==
''Plectranthus hadiensis'' is widely used as an [[ornamental plant]] because it is easy to cultivate, propagate and maintain. The compounds of the plant were formerly used to poison fish and more traditionally as an [[enema]]. It is used to ward off evil spirits. In Uganda it is used to heal wounds and peptic ulcers.
== Properties ==
The plant's use as a [[pharmacological agent]] is being investigated as it contains large quantities of [[essential oils]], it is also being investigated for use against [[respiratory infections]].{{citation needed|date=January 2021}} However, ointments made with compounds extracted from the plant must not contain [[menthol]], [[camphor]] or [[eucalyptus]].<ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.9729/AM.2013.43.1.34|title = Ambient Variable Pressure Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy for Trichome Profiling of Plectranthus tomentosa by Secondary Electron Imaging|year = 2013|last1 = Kim|first1 = Ki Woo|journal = Applied Microscopy|volume = 43|pages = 34–39|doi-access = free}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
''Plectranthus hadiensis'' was discovered by [[Peter Forsskål]] in Hadiyah, [[Yemen]]. It was [[Species description|described]] in ''Flora of Egypt and Arabia'' in 1775 with the name ''Ocimum hadiensis''. At that time the genus ''[[Plectranthus]]'' had not been established, however it was the first species of the genus described and in 1894 the botanists [[Georg August Schweinfurth|Schweinfurth]] and [[Carl Ludwig Sprenger|Sprenger]] transferred it to the new genus, publishing it in ''[[Wiener Illustrirte Garten-Zeitung]]'' 19: 2. 1894.<ref name="Trop">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=''Plectranthus hadiensis''|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/17602756|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=18 October 2014|website=Tropicos.org.
